data.hypothesis: Expanding the selected 16-row tile to 32 output rows while keeping 32 contiguous X lanes and eight Y threads should reduce Y blocks per plane and amortize halo loads: the cooperative tile is 40 rows for 32 outputs (1.25 loaded rows/output versus 24/16 for the parent). The same 256-thread block performs four outputs per thread and uses about 5 KiB shared memory, so extra per-thread work or occupancy effects may offset the reuse benefit; measure rather than assume a speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: This larger-tile experiment tests the tradeoff on the same fixed 64-row domain and target; its timing and oracle validity are still unmeasured.
memory_lessons.claim: The 16-row parent was oracle-correct and measured at 3.2230 µs versus the 3.5815 µs baseline, but its three sample times ranged from 2.6003 to 3.5818 µs, so the mean alone does not establish a robust tile-height advantage.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare repeated official full-run timings for this 32-row tile against baseline and parent; if larger per-thread work offsets reuse, contrast with a smaller tile.

data.notes: This is a contrasting tile-height experiment, not a claimed improvement. For the stated 64-row Y extent it halves the Y grid from four blocks to two per X/Z block and initializes all 40 tile rows; the existing q<0 / q>63 convention leaves index 63 unchanged. The parent and baseline timings have noticeable sample variability. Candidate oracle checks on signed varying inputs with independent endpoint values and repeated official full-run measurements remain pending controller evaluation.
transformations: Increase the shared-memory Y output tile from 16 to 32 rows while retaining a 32-lane contiguous-X dimension and eight Y threads per block.
Cooperatively initialize all 40 shared rows, including halos; each thread loads five rows and computes four output rows after the barrier.
Use the resulting two Y blocks per 64-row plane while preserving the stencil coefficients, full output writes, inputs, scratch behavior, and exact q<0 / q>63 wrapping convention.
